articles.title: 400 km, five districts and two years: The remarkable journey of a young tiger searching for a place to call home
articles.summary: Animals & Pets News: A young tiger has turned into one of Maharashtra’s most unexpected long-distance travellers. The big cat, believed to have originated in Tipeshwar Wil.
articles.body: A young tiger has turned into one of Maharashtra’s most unexpected long-distance travellers. The big cat, believed to have originated in Tipeshwar Wildlife Sanctuary in Yavatmal, has been moving across central Maharashtra for nearly two years. It was recently photographed in Beed, more than 400 km from its original habitat, before disappearing from surveillance for several days.It has now been traced again in neighbouring Dharashiv district.The tiger was not ‘lost’ in the usual senseThe word “missing” can make the story sound like a tiger escaped from a zoo or was being searched for after captivity. That is not what happened here.The animal is wild and has been moving through forests and hilly landscapes on its own. Forest officials had camera traps in place to monitor its movements, but no images were recorded for nearly 10 days after its last confirmed sighting.That gap ended on August 29, when the tiger was traced near Yeswandi in Vashi tehsil of Dharashiv.How its 400-km journey unfoldedThe tiger was first spotted in the Ashti hills of Beed on December 10, 2025. It appeared there again on July 27, 2026.Then came a cattle kill in Brahmagaon on August 13. Following the incident, the forest department increased surveillance and installed camera traps. The tiger was photographed on August 20.After that, there was silence.Nearly 10 days later, officials detected the animal again near Yeswandi. It is now moving along the Terkheda-Yeswandi stretch around the Bhoom and Dharashiv borders.Why did the tiger travel so far?Tigers naturally need large territories, particularly young males looking for suitable areas to establish themselves. But this journey is significant because the animal has crossed several districts while apparently finding enough food and water to continue moving.According to forest officials, the tiger has explored parts of Beed, Latur, Dharashiv, Solapur and Ahilyanagar during the past two years.Its prolonged presence also suggests that parts of this landscape can support a large carnivore. Officials have pointed to the availability of prey and water as important reasons for its continued movement through the region.The forest corridor may be the bigger storyThe tiger’s journey tells a story larger than one wandering animal.Its movement provides evidence that the natural corridor between Tipeshwar and Yedshi Ramling Ghat Wildlife Sanctuary is still functioning. Wildlife corridors allow animals to move between habitats instead of becoming trapped in isolated forest patches.The Yedshi region has now emerged as an important centre of the tiger’s wide-ranging movements. Officials believe it may continue towards Naldurg and Yedshi.As Range Forest Officer Amol Munde said, “The tiger is currently roaming the Terkheda-Yeswandi stretch along the Bhoom and Dharashiv borders and is likely moving towards Naldurg and Yedshi.”For a tiger, a 400-km journey is not simply a remarkable distance. It is a reminder that wildlife does not recognise the boundaries drawn on a map. When forests, water sources and prey remain connected, animals can still find their way across landscapes that humans consider separate.Disclaimer: This article is based on information reported by PTI and statements attributed to Maharashtra forest officials. The tiger’s exact route, age and identity have not been publicly established in the cited report beyond its reported origin from Tipeshwar Wildlife Sanctuary.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: ‘We would have had real civil strife’: JD Vance recalls 2024 attack on Trump
articles.summary: US News: US Vice President JD Vance said in a podcast released Tuesday (local time) that he feared a “real civil strife” had a 2024 attempt on Donald Trump’s l.
articles.body: US Vice President JD Vance said in a podcast released Tuesday (local time) that he feared a “real civil strife” had a 2024 attempt on Donald Trump’s life been successful.Vance made the remarks during a conversation with Christian podcaster Bryce Crawford. During the conversation, he cited the July 13, 2024, assassination attempt in Butler, Pennsylvania, during which a bullet whizzed past Trump’s ear before striking a supporter, who was killed. The gunman, Thomas Matthew Crooks, was shot dead by Secret Service snipers.“We would have had real civil strife in a way that I don't know that the country could have ever come back from. There would have just been an illegitimacy to our entire political system,” the Associated Press quoted the vice president as saying.Vance further stated that, like many other Trump supporters, he too would have suspected a conspiracy had Crooks been successful.“I would have assumed very dark forces had taken out Donald Trump, right as he was about to come back into the White House. Many Trump supporters would have assumed a conspiracy had robbed them of their chosen president... I would have also had those thoughts 'in the back of my mind,'” he added.On July 15, 2024, Trump formally announced Vance as his running mate, or vice presidential candidate. In the November 2024 election, the Trump-Vance Republican ticket defeated the Democratic ticket of Kamala Harris and her running mate, Tim Walz.Vance on Trump's AI-generated image as Jesus ChristCrawford also asked Vance about a social media post Trump shared earlier this year featuring an AI-generated image of himself as Jesus, which the podcast host described as offensive. Trump initially contended that he thought the image depicted him as a doctor, but later removed the post amid widespread criticism, including from some of his own supporters.Vance defended the president, arguing that Trump did not intend to “mock or mimic God” and that “that's just not who he is.” He added that Trump often tries to keep things light and frequently jokes. “He's a bit of a ballbuster, for those of us who work with him, and he just likes to have a good time,” Vance remarked. “And I think that if people appreciated that, they would recognize, he's not trying to offend people, he's trying to keep things light.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Times Square stabbing: Bank of America VP Erin Piacenti among victims
articles.summary: US News: A 32-year-old vice-president at Bank of America was killed in a stabbing incident in New York’s Times Square. The attack, described by police as “rand.
articles.body: A 32-year-old vice-president at Bank of America was killed in a stabbing incident in New York’s Times Square. The attack, described by police as “random” and unprovoked, unfolded on Monday afternoon.The victim was identified as Erin Piacenti, who was walking home from work when she was attacked near West 42nd Street and Seventh Avenue. Piacenti had recently returned to work after becoming a mother and had shared a photo of herself with her newborn daughter and husband four days before the stabbing.A 68-year-old man was also stabbed in the attack and was in stable condition, according to police. The attacker, identified as 49-year-old Pamela Cisneros, was shot and killed by officers after she advanced towards them while carrying two large knives.Who was Erin Piacenti?Piacenti was a vice-president in Bank of America’s Business Selection and Conflicts unit and had joined the company around 18 months ago, according to an internal memo and her LinkedIn profile.Matthew Koder, Bank of America’s president of Global Corporate & Investment Banking, described Piacenti as a “cherished teammate and friend” in an internal memo.“Erin was a valued member of the Business Selection and Conflicts team, having joined the bank 18 months ago,” Koder wrote. “Her loss is being felt deeply by many.”Bank of America confirmed Piacenti’s death and expressed condolences to her family.“We are shocked and deeply saddened by the tragic loss of our colleague. She was a valued teammate who will be greatly missed. Our hearts go out to her family and all of her loved ones,” the bank said in a statement.Piacenti had earned a law degree from Fordham Law School, graduating in 2021 alongside her husband, Frank, according to the school. Fordham Law said in a statement it was heartbroken by her death.Bank of America’s Manhattan office is located at One Bryant Park, just a few blocks from the site of the stabbing.How the incident unfoldedNYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch said the attack appeared to be random and unprovoked. Police identified the attacker as Pamela Cisneros, 49, of Queens.According to Tisch, Cisneros pulled two knives from a shopping bag, stabbed the 68-year-old man and then attacked Piacenti. When officers arrived, they found Cisneros brandishing two large knives and advancing towards them.Officers used a stun gun and tried to persuade her to drop the weapons for several minutes, but she refused. Tisch said Cisneros told officers she “would rather kill” them. Two officers then shot her, and she was later pronounced dead.Tisch said Cisneros had a documented mental health history, with police encounters related to mental health in 2018 and 2019, but no arrest record in New York City.Cisneros’ brother, Patrick Peralta, told Gothamist that she had psychiatric problems for decades but was not aggressive. He said she had been taking medication and had been doing better in recent years, working on and off in a legal office.“We really don’t know how to express or how to explain why this happened," Peralta told Gothamist, expressing sympathy for Piacenti’s family and the injured man.Koder said Bank of America’s security teams were “fully engaged in supporting the police investigation here, and in addressing the ongoing safety and security of our offices and teammates”.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Hong Kong’s pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong pleads guilty to association with foreign entities
articles.summary: China News: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong, 29, pleaded guilty on Wednesday to a national security allegation of collusion with foreign entities, an off.
articles.body: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong, 29, pleaded guilty on Wednesday to a national security allegation of collusion with foreign entities, an offence that carries a potential life sentence. Several Western diplomats were present at the hearing.Wong rose to international prominence as a teenage pro-democracy activist, part of a generation of young protesters whose activism has since been effectively criminalised under the sweeping National Security Law that Beijing imposed on Hong Kong in 2020.According to a charge sheet seen by Reuters, prosecutors accused Wong of conspiring with exiled activist Nathan Law and others to solicit foreign countries, institutions, organisations, or individuals to impose sanctions or blockades against Hong Kong and China. The alleged conduct occurred between July 1 and November 23, 2020. Wong was arrested on these charges in June 2025, the second time he has faced prosecution under the National Security Law.During the hearing, prosecutors emphasised an alleged international media and political campaign led by Demosisto, a now-disbanded political party Wong once led, that had advocated for a referendum on Hong Kong's sovereignty. The campaign reportedly sought sanctions against Hong Kong and China in 2019 and 2020.Wong is currently serving a sentence from an earlier national security conviction, conspiracy to commit subversion, stemming from his participation in an unofficial 2020 primary election among democratic activists. That sentence is due to end next year.The National Security Law was enacted on June 30, 2020, partly in response to the often-violent pro-democracy protests that engulfed Hong Kong in 2019.International human rights organisations and Western governments have criticised the law as excessive, arguing it undermines the high degree of autonomy promised to Hong Kong after its 1997 handover from British to Chinese rule.Hong Kong and Chinese authorities, however, maintain the law was necessary to restore stability.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Leeds weather forecast: Heavy rain and cooler temperatures expected Tuesday, September 2, 2026
articles.summary: UK News: Leeds residents are bracing for a wet start to the week with heavy rain forecast for Tuesday, September 2, 2026. Temperatures will also see a noticeab.
articles.body: Leeds residents are bracing for a wet start to the week with heavy rain forecast for Tuesday, September 2, 2026. Temperatures will also see a noticeable drop. The outlook for the rest of the week indicates a gradual improvement with sunny intervals expected from Wednesday onwards, leading to warmer and more settled conditions by the weekend.Detailed Tuesday ForecastToday, Tuesday, September 2, 2026, Leeds will experience persistent heavy rain. The high temperature is predicted to be 19°C, with a low of 16°C, making the average temperature around 17.5°C. The chance of rain is high, and humidity will reach 95%.Wind speeds are expected to reach up to 37.01 kph. The day is forecast to be overcast and wet, with minimal sunshine.Residents are advised to carry umbrellas and wear waterproof footwear if they plan to go outdoors. The high humidity and precipitation will contribute to damp and potentially chilly conditions.Outdoor activities may need to be adjusted, and indoor alternatives should be considered. Commuters should also anticipate potential delays due to the adverse weather.Mid-Week ImprovementLooking ahead, Wednesday, September 3, will bring sunny intervals. Temperatures are expected to range from 14°C to 20°C.This pattern of sunny intervals is set to continue through Thursday, September 4, and Friday, September 5. Maximum temperatures will be around 19°C and 18°C respectively. Minimum temperatures will drop to 12°C and 11°C.Warmer Weekend AheadThe weekend forecast shows a pleasant change. Saturday, September 6, is expected to have sunny intervals with a warmer high of 23°C and a low of 14°C. Sunday, September 7, will also feature sunny intervals, with a high of 19°C and a low of 13°C. The latter half of the week promises more settled and warmer weather following Tuesday's heavy rain.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 1995, Clint Eastwood sold a large California property for $3.08 million; the land was placed under permanent conservation protection instead of being developed
articles.summary: US News: In 1995, actor and filmmaker Clint Eastwood sold roughly 280 acres of his California coastal property to Monterey County for $3.08 million, helping en.
articles.body: In 1995, actor and filmmaker Clint Eastwood sold roughly 280 acres of his California coastal property to Monterey County for $3.08 million, helping ensure that a large stretch of scenic land would remain undeveloped. The property, associated with Eastwood’s long-held Malpaso holdings near Carmel Highlands, was divided into five parcels and was acquired by the county for open-space preservation. Rather than becoming available for future construction, the land was placed under a conservation easement intended to protect it permanently. The transaction formed part of a wider conservation effort around Carmel and the Carmel River, where several important coastal properties were facing development pressure. Eastwood’s role in the episode was more complicated than a simple donation, since the county purchased the land, but the resulting protection prevented its future development.Clint Eastwood’s long connection to the landEastwood began acquiring property around Malpaso Creek in the late 1960s, building a substantial collection of land along the rugged Monterey County coast. Contemporary accounts reported that his broader holdings in the area eventually covered roughly 650 acres, although the portion involved in the 1995 county transaction was considerably smaller. Eastwood had purchased land in the area during a period when development was increasingly changing parts of the Carmel region, while the coastal landscape around Malpaso Creek retained large areas of undeveloped terrain. The property’s location along Highway 1 and near the Big Sur coast also gave it considerable scenic and environmental importance.The $3.08 million saleIn 1995, Monterey County purchased approximately 279 to 280 acres of Eastwood’s Malpaso property for $3.08 million. The land consisted of five parcels and was acquired for open-space purposes. Contemporary reporting connected the transaction to California’s Proposition 70, a state bond measure that provided money for acquiring and protecting open space. The deal therefore involved a direct purchase rather than a straightforward charitable donation by Eastwood. The distinction matters because the conservation result came through a public acquisition in which the county became the owner of the property.The land was protected from future developmentOne of the most significant aspects of the transaction was what happened after the county acquired the property. The Malpaso land was subject to a conservation easement that required its protection in perpetuity. The restriction was designed to prevent the county’s ownership from later being converted into a development opportunity. The arrangement meant that the property could remain open space rather than being subdivided or built over. Contemporary reporting also noted that the land was not simply turned into a conventional public park, with questions surrounding public access remaining separate from the permanent protection of the property itself.The property had been facing a very different futureThe significance of the acquisition becomes clearer when viewed against the development pressures affecting the Carmel area at the time. Nearby land around the Carmel River was also being considered for residential development, prompting conservation groups and local authorities to look for ways to preserve remaining open spaces. The Malpaso transaction became connected to a broader series of property deals involving the Eastwoods, Monterey County and the Big Sur Land Trust. Together, those efforts helped protect several hundred acres of environmentally and scenically important land around the Carmel coast.The deal was linked to the fight over Odello RanchThe 1995 Malpaso sale was particularly important because it was intertwined with the preservation of the nearby Odello Ranch, a former artichoke-growing property at the mouth of the Carmel River. Development plans had proposed dozens of homes on the approximately 134-acre property. The Eastwoods subsequently became involved in the complicated effort surrounding the site, purchasing the property after a development option was abandoned. The episode eventually helped lead to the preservation of much of the land rather than the residential development originally contemplated.Eastwood later helped protect more coastal landThe conservation story did not end with the Malpaso transaction. In 1997, Eastwood and Maggie Johnson announced an arrangement involving the transfer of substantial Coast Ranch land to the Big Sur Land Trust. Contemporary reports valued the property involved at about $6 million and said the arrangement would keep most of the land from being developed. The deal included restrictions affecting development rights and helped preserve open space around the Carmel River. The preservation effort also involved Monterey County land retained for flood-control purposes and agricultural protections on other portions of the property.The financial side of the Malpaso deal drew scrutinyThe transaction was not without controversy. A later investigation by Coast Weekly examined the financial circumstances surrounding the Malpaso purchase and noted that Monterey County records had placed the property’s assessed value at about $308,682 in July 1994, far below the $3.08 million purchase price. That difference alone does not establish that the county overpaid, since a tax assessment is not necessarily the same as a property’s market value or its value for conservation purposes. However, the disparity became part of the scrutiny surrounding the transaction. The investigation also reported that county officials did not have a record of what Eastwood had originally paid for the property.Conservationists saw both benefits and complicationsThe wider Eastwood land deals generated debate among conservationists and others involved in Monterey County land-use policy. Supporters pointed to the substantial amount of coastal and riverfront land that ultimately escaped development. Critics, meanwhile, questioned the financial and development-rights arrangements involved in the transactions, particularly around Odello Ranch. The debate illustrates that conservation victories involving private landowners and public authorities can involve complicated exchanges of property, development rights, water rights and tax considerations. Even with those disputes, the physical conservation outcome was significant because large areas that had faced development pressure were ultimately placed under long-term protection.Malpaso Creek made the land environmentally significantThe Malpaso property was valuable not only because of its dramatic coastal scenery but also because of its ecological setting. Malpaso Creek runs through the rugged Carmel Highlands landscape before reaching the Pacific, while the surrounding region contains important coastal habitats and Monterey pine forest. Monterey County planning documents have identified the Malpaso area as having significant conservation value, including its importance to Monterey pine habitat. Protecting undeveloped land in this landscape therefore helped preserve more than a scenic backdrop. It also maintained a relatively intact portion of a sensitive coastal environment where development could have fragmented habitat and altered the character of the landscape.It was a sale rather than a celebrity land donationThe distinction between a sale and a donation is central to telling the story accurately. Eastwood did not simply give the roughly 280 acres to Monterey County for free. The county paid $3.08 million to acquire the five parcels, with Proposition 70 funding playing a role in the open-space acquisition. What makes the episode a conservation story is what happened through and after that purchase. The land was acquired for preservation and subjected to a permanent conservation restriction, removing the possibility of ordinary future development.A larger conservation legacy around CarmelThe Malpaso transaction became one part of a broader pattern of land preservation associated with Eastwood’s property interests around Carmel. His involvement with the Mission Ranch, his earlier land transactions in Carmel Valley and the later preservation of land connected to Odello Ranch all contributed to a complicated local history in which privately held property was repeatedly at the centre of debates over development and conservation. The 1995 sale stands out because it converted roughly 280 acres of Eastwood’s coastal holdings into county-owned open space protected by a permanent conservation easement.The strongest legacy of the transaction is therefore not simply that a Hollywood star owned a large piece of California. It is that a substantial portion of his Malpaso property changed hands through a public conservation purchase at a time when development pressure was affecting the Carmel coast. Roughly 279 to 280 acres were sold for $3.08 million and placed under permanent conservation protection, ensuring that the land would not follow the conventional path from private ownership to subdivision and construction. The surrounding transactions were financially and politically complicated, but the central conservation outcome remains clear. A large area of environmentally and scenically important coastal land was secured as protected open space rather than developed.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Pennsylvania police shooting: Officer charged in death of college student
articles.summary: US News: A Pennsylvania police officer has been charged with voluntary manslaughter after shooting and killing a 22-year-old college student who had wound up a.
articles.body: A Pennsylvania police officer has been charged with voluntary manslaughter after shooting and killing a 22-year-old college student who had wound up at the incorrect residence late at night while waiting for friends to pick him up, stated by the prosecutor on Tuesday.Upper Pottsgrove Police Cpl. Sean Farrell, 58, is accused of Glenwood Earl Pysher IV's death in August 23, according to Montgomery County District Attorney Kevin Steele. The officer did not have to kill Pysher during the confrontation since officer had less-lethal choices, according to the prosecuter.According to a news statement from the district attorney's office, the Montgomery County Detective Bureau looked into the shooting and examined video from Farrell's body-worn camera.According to the inquiry, "Cpl. Farrell had a taser and other less-lethal weapons on his utility belt that he did not use. The victim had his hands raised and was not carrying a weapon at the time of the shot, and the officer was safely behind a vehicle from Pysher. There was no danger from Mr. Pysher. This is not a legal use of deadly force, leading to the charge of Voluntary Manslaughter," as per the news release from Steele.Pysher's family lawyer thanked the prosecution in a statement.Attorney Ken Fulginiti stated, "The family is grateful for the work of the Montgomery County District Attorney's office and they are looking forward to justice in this horribly tragic, preventable, and reckless conduct that took their son's life."On Tuesday, Farrell surrendered to the Montgomery County Detectives. According to a district attorney's office representative, Farrell must surrender all firearms to the state police in order to be released after Magisterial District Judge Kathleen Rebar set bail at $75,000. On September 10, he will have a preliminary hearing.When a resident contacted 911 to report someone attempting to break into a home through the rear door, Farrell was the first officer on the scene. According to the statement, Farrell's body-worn video captured the officer moving down the driveway with his gun drawn and illuminating the path with its light.Farrell noticed Pysher on the patio of the house, close to the back door, while standing behind a car in the driveway. "Police, let me see your hands," shouted Farrell. "Hands up, hands up now, drop to the ground," he then shouted.According to the statement, Pysher was seen on camera raising his hands as he started to approach the officer and kept going in that way as the officer ordered, "Drop to the ground." "Drop to the ground," Farrell yelled once more, followed by "Stop or I'll..." However, according to the district attorney's office, Farrell fired two rounds before he could complete the sentence, striking Pysher twice in the chest.According to the announcement, Pysher was shot between 17 and 20 feet (5 and 6 meters) away from the officer.Pysher had been out at many pubs earlier in the evening to celebrate a friend's 21st birthday, according to the inquiry. Around 11 p.m., a designated driver took the party to the birthday person's house. About 30 minutes later, Pysher exited to walk half a mile to another friend's house to continue drinking, but he ended up at the incorrect residence, according to the release. Based on what his son's friends have told him, Pysher's father has stated that he thinks his son attempted to enter what he believed to be his friend's home.Glen Pysher told The Associated Press last week that "his son tried to open the doorknob and obviously startled the homeowner." According to what we know, he said, "He believed he was at his friend's house, so he said, "Hey! Open the door!"The father said that after his son sat down on the back porch and called his buddies, they noticed he was in the wrong area and started looking for him.Philip Stinson, a criminal justice professor at Bowling Green State University, maintains a national database of almost 25,000 police officer arrests since 2005.Stinson's research shows that between January 2005 and the end of July 2026, 218 local sworn police officers were charged with either murder or manslaughter in a fatal police shot that occurred while they were on duty. Although there are still a number of unresolved cases, 78 policemen have been found guilty, while 107 have been found not guilty or discharged.During that period, ten cops in Pennsylvania were accused, six of them were found guilty.According to Stinson, there have been variations in the number of cops charged over time, but those variations are statistically minor considering that there are about a thousand fatal police confrontations annually."These are ugly situations. "The facts are never simple," Stinson said. Criminal juries and grand juries appear to have similar problems. In a potentially violent street confrontation, they are hesitant to question the split-second, frequently life-or-death judgments made by an on-duty police officer.Most cops involved in deadly on-duty shootings shot an unarmed victim. Just ten of the victims in the 78 convictions had guns when they were shot.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
